chosen.premise: When moisture wrinkles Sandshrew’s skin, it travels to a volcano and lies on geothermal heat to dry out.
chosen.hook: If Sandshrew gets wrinkled by moisture, it heads straight for a volcano.
chosen.visualIdea: Morph Sandshrew from a wrinkled, damp state into a flat silhouette basking on a glowing geothermal spot.
chosen.note: The single-entry premise is exceptionally specific, strange, memorable, and directly supported: moisture wrinkles its skin, so it uses geothermal heat to dry itself.

candidates.premise: When Sandshrew curls into a ball, attacks bounce off—and it can even survive a great fall by bouncing.
candidates.hook: Sandshrew’s emergency move is turning itself into a bouncing ball.
candidates.visualIdea: Drop a curled Sandshrew, show it bounce, then have incoming attacks ricochet harmlessly away.
candidates.note: A highly visual defensive mechanic unique to Sandshrew, though “any attack” and surviving a great fall are broad Pokédex claims rather than precisely defined limits.

candidates.premise: Sandshrew bathes in dry grit to remove dirt and moisture clinging to its body.
candidates.hook: Sandshrew doesn’t bathe in water—it uses sand to get clean.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Sandshrew rolling through grit as droplets and dirt visibly peel away from its hide.
candidates.note: Strongly supported and easy to depict, but sand bathing is a less surprising hook than the volcano behavior and overlaps with Sandshrew’s expected desert identity.

candidates.premise: Sandshrew dislikes water, yet its body absorbs it without waste to survive in the desert.
candidates.hook: Sandshrew hates water—but its body is built to save every drop.
candidates.visualIdea: Show water repelled by Sandshrew, then animate each absorbed drop being conserved in a desert survival meter.
candidates.note: The water aversion versus water-conservation contradiction is strong and well supported, but the proposed water-repelling visual conflicts with the claim that Sandshrew absorbs water.
